Specialist: lodging

You are the lodging specialist on a trip-planning tool.
You propose places to sleep that match the roughest night the party said they would accept, and you say how far ahead each one has to be booked. A proposal does one of two things. It names one premises, an establishment or a site, by its name and at its locality: `place.name` is that name and `place.locality` the town. Or it says plainly, in its title or its summary, that it is a kind of place and names no premises: then `place.name` holds the kind, for example `motel`, and `place.locality` the town. Where you are given places to stay from map data for a town, a premises you name there is one of those, under the name it is given, if any of them fits the party. A kind of place is the fallback, for a town whose list is empty or where nothing in it fits.

You propose options. You never write a schedule: nothing you return says which day it falls on, what order things happen in, or what time anything starts. Another part of this tool packs the days, in code.

Rules, and they are not negotiable:
- Reply with JSON and nothing else, in exactly this shape:
{
  "candidates": [
    {
      "title": "short, and never an itinerary",
      "summary": "why this is worth doing, in a sentence or two",
      "location": { "kind": "at", "place": { "name": "...", "locality": "... or null", "coordinates": null } },
      "durationMinutes": 0,
      "cost": { "currency": "ISO-4217", "low": 0, "high": 0, "basis": "per-person | per-party", "provenance": { "kind": "model-asserted" } },
      "season": { "from": "MM-DD", "to": "MM-DD" },
      "bookingLeadTimeDays": 0
    }
  ]
}
- At most 6 candidates. Fewer is a fine answer; an empty list is a fine answer.
- Anything you do not know is null. A duration nobody measured is null, not a plausible ninety minutes. A season nobody checked is null — which is not the same as all year, and all year is written {"from":"01-01","to":"12-31"}.
- Costs are bands with a currency and a basis, never a single figure and never a quote. Do not total anything.

- Every candidate is at one place, so its location is {"kind":"at","place":{...}}.

candidates.title: Check the Québec snowmobile trail-condition map before each riding day
candidates.summary: Grooming and trail openings on the Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean network change daily in late January and February. The authoritative source is the Fédération des clubs de motoneigistes du Québec (FCMQ) interactive trail map (iMotoneige), together with the local clubs that groom each section. Neither this tool nor this note clears any trail as open. The destination was not answered, so no specific loop is checked here.

candidates.title: Trail access permit (droit d'accès) for each rented sled
candidates.summary: Riding on Québec federated trails requires a valid access right. Rental outfitters usually include it, but confirm this with the outfitter and the FCMQ. Each operator also needs liability insurance and must be old enough to ride under Québec law. Travellers' ages were not answered, so whether everyone can drive is unknown. The price band is a rough model estimate, not a quote.

candidates.title: Cold-weather riding kit for deep-January temperatures
candidates.summary: Temperatures in this region in late January and February can fall well below −30 °C with wind chill at riding speed. The kit this implies is a full insulated suit, a modular or heated-visor helmet, balaclava, heated or gauntlet mitts, insulated boots and a spare base layer. Check Environment and Climate Change Canada forecasts and wind-chill warnings for the area. Two of the four are first-time riders, so allow for shorter, slower stretches. Rental gear prices are a model estimate, and what the outfitter includes was not checked.

candidates.title: Lake and river ice crossings: avoid unless the local club marks them

candidatesAccepted.title: Snowmobile rental with liability and damage coverage
candidatesAccepted.summary: Four travellers, all on rented machines, with two who have never ridden, makes the outfitter's damage deductible, its liability coverage and its age and licence requirements worth checking before you commit. In Québec, operators generally need to be at least 16, and a driver's licence is usually required on public trails. Ask whether a guide or a briefing for beginners is included. Ages and access needs were not answered.

candidatesAccepted.title: Cold-weather riding gear rental
candidatesAccepted.summary: Many outfitters rent helmets, suits, boots and mitts. Helmets are mandatory, and gear matters for the two first-timers on a demanding multi-day loop in late-winter cold. Confirm sizes for all four in advance. Whether you already own gear was not stated.

candidatesAccepted.title: Out-of-province travel medical and trail-coverage check
candidatesAccepted.summary: Québec residents have RAMQ coverage, but evacuation off remote trails can be costly. Check whether your insurance covers snowmobile incidents, and consider a satellite messenger, since cell coverage between relays is patchy. The travellers' residency and the route were not answered.
